# psv_rom_tool

[← Command index](README.md)

Strip, unstrip, trim, untrim or verify PlayStation Vita cartridge dumps (.psv).

## Synopsis

```
psv_rom_tool [options]
```

## Description

Finds every `.psv` file under the input path (or takes the one file given) and applies
one action to each. New files are written next to the source:

- `-s` strips the dump with PSVStrip into `<name>_stripped.psv`.
- `-u` rebuilds a full dump from a stripped one and the `<name>.psve` file next to it
  with PSVStrip, into `<name>_unstripped.psv`.
- `-t` trims the unused space with PSVTools into `<name>_trimmed.psv`.
- `-n` expands a trimmed dump back to full size with PSVTools into
  `<name>_untrimmed.psv`.
- `-e` runs the PSVTools check on each dump and writes nothing.

With `-d` the source `.psv` is deleted after each successful strip, unstrip, trim or
untrim.

## Options

### General

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-i, --input_path <input_path>` | A `.psv` file, or a directory searched recursively for them; must exist. |

### Actions

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-s, --strip` | Strip each dump into `<name>_stripped.psv`. |
| `-u, --unstrip` | Rebuild each stripped dump from it and `<name>.psve` into `<name>_unstripped.psv`. |
| `-t, --trim` | Trim each dump into `<name>_trimmed.psv`. |
| `-n, --untrim` | Expand each trimmed dump to full size into `<name>_untrimmed.psv`. |
| `-e, --verify` | Check each dump with PSVTools without writing anything. |

### Behavior

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-d, --delete_originals` | Delete the source `.psv` after it is converted; ignored by `-e`. |

### Common options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-v, --verbose` | Enable verbose mode. |
| `-p, --pretend_run` | Do a pretend run with no permanent changes. |
| `-x, --exit_on_failure` | Enable exit on failure mode. |
| `--no-preview` | Skip the preview confirmation prompt. |

## Examples

### Verify every dump in a folder

```bash
psv_rom_tool -i /path/to/psv -e
```

### Trim every dump and delete the untrimmed originals

```bash
psv_rom_tool -i /path/to/psv -t -d
```

### Preview the trim without changing anything

```bash
psv_rom_tool -i /path/to/psv -t -d -p -v
```

### Rebuild a full dump from a stripped one and its .psve

```bash
psv_rom_tool -i "/path/to/Game (USA).psv" -u
```

## Notes

- Give one action. When several are given, only the first in the order `-s`, `-u`, `-t`, `-n`, `-e` is used.
- Output files are also `.psv`, so running the tool again on the same folder processes them too.
- PSVStrip, and PSVTools with the JoyBox Python environment, must be installed as JoyBox tools.
